sections.vendors: John Lewis Partnership published its Ethics and Sustainability Report 2025/26. The brand became the first UK retailer to source Physical BCI Cotton from Egypt under BCI's new Chain of Custody standard — a significant provenance differentiation from mass-market BCI users. JLP is working towards fully certified cashmere across key suppliers.
sections.sustainability: JLP achieved a 40% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions against its 2020/21 baseline in 2025. The brand is committing to zero-deforestation and conversion-free sourcing of key commodities including cotton, cashmere, and polyester across own-brand supply chains. Recycled polyester reporting has been added to the brand's sustainability metrics.
sections.sourcing: John Lewis sources premium fabrics from Portugal (Somelos Tecidos), Scotland (Johnstons of Elgin for wool/cashmere), India (Arvind Mills), and Sri Lanka (MAS Holdings). The brand's emphasis on GOTS organic, RWS wool, and now BCI Physical Egypt cotton reflects its premium sourcing positioning.
sections.strategy: John Lewis is piloting an app-based garment buy-back service, allowing customers to schedule home pickups of John Lewis-purchased garments in return for payment — regardless of condition. This circular economy initiative positions JLP as a premium resale and circular loop partner.
sections.pricing: John Lewis maintains a premium pricing position in UK clothing, supported by its Never Knowingly Undersold legacy and quality-fabric positioning. The brand continues to compete on product quality and sustainability credentials rather than price.
sections.launches: JLP AW2026 collections featured an expanded circular economy framework — new collections are designed with end-of-life take-back in mind. The Johnnie B kidswear and John Lewis own-brand ranges incorporated more GOTS organic cotton and RWS wool than prior seasons.
sections.gossip: The buy-back app pilot is generating significant press interest as a potential differentiator for John Lewis in premium circular fashion. Industry watchers note that JLP's partnership retail model (selling third-party brands alongside own-label) complicates a fully circular own-brand narrative.
soWhat: Physical BCI Cotton from Egypt sourcing signals John Lewis's willingness to pay a premium for differentiated raw material provenance — suppliers who can source and certify origin-specific cotton (Egyptian, Supima, etc.) can command a premium with JLP buyers

Zero-deforestation commitment for cashmere and polyester means John Lewis will increase scrutiny of supplier sourcing chains — cashmere suppliers must demonstrate certified pastureland management; polyester suppliers must transition to GRS recycled

The buy-back/circular initiative means John Lewis is building a closed-loop value proposition — suppliers who co-design for disassembly, durability and fibre recoverability will be strategically valued partners for JLP's circular future
